correctness.rationale: Necessity is witnessed by the r-state full-range effectivity frame. Sufficiency follows from the explicit mixed-modulus array: for fixed coordinate i<k choose the largest coordinate to hit the desired ith residue and then solve all remaining residues; for fixed maximum coordinate choose other coordinates independently. Any surjection of its image to the local union is slice-surjective. The fallback-in-intersection outcome rule has attainable set precisely each fixed agent action's selected neighborhood. The proof covers every finite k>=2 and r>=1. Bundled checks independently reconstruct all neighborhood images in 463 finite instances and test 1486 slice configurations; no inference from enumeration to infinity.

value.rationale: This is the complete finite universal feasible-region classification for heterogeneous per-agent action multiplicities, not a routine change in a single integer. Agent budgets can differ due to asymmetric resource constraints, and the exact product condition identifies admissible tradeoffs and infeasible profiles without an optimization search. The small (2,3,3) versus (3,3,3) example exhibits a genuine budget saving unavailable from the previously published uniform construction. The proof gives a reusable constructive mixed-modulus slice lemma and a matching worst-case obstruction.
